title: Diwali Bonuses Fuel Festive Rush Across Nashik's Markets
excerpt: An estimated Rs 500 crore in factory bonuses is reaching nearly one lakh Nashik workers this week, and the city's garment, gold and auto markets are feeling it first.
body:
• Nashik's main markets saw heavy Diwali footfall on Tuesday as factory bonuses and monthly salaries reached workers' accounts.
  • Industry body NIMA estimates about Rs 500 crore in bonuses will be paid to nearly one lakh workers across more than 3,500 industrial units in the Satpur and Ambad MIDC estates.
  • Bonuses this year range from Rs 15,000 to Rs 1.25 lakh, and spending is flowing to garments, gold, automobiles, electronics and home appliances.
  • Cloth merchants say the rush picked up from November 1, though shoppers remain cautious about prices.

Nashik's shopping districts were crowded on Tuesday evening as residents spent Diwali bonuses and monthly salaries on clothes, sweets and festive goods, with traders expecting the rush to build further before Diwali on November 8.

Shoppers filled the city's traditional commercial hubs — Main Road, MG Road, Shalimar, Saraf Bazaar, Kapada Market and Raviwar Karanja — buying garments, lanterns, diyas, decorative items, sweets, dry fruits, gift articles and household essentials, The Times of India reported.

Rs 500 crore in bonuses, by industry estimate

Ashish Nahar, president of the Nashik Industries and Manufacturers Association (NIMA), estimated that about Rs 500 crore would be disbursed as Diwali bonuses to nearly one lakh workers in more than 3,500 industrial units in the Satpur and Ambad MIDC estates, within Nashik Municipal Corporation limits. Bonuses this year range from Rs 15,000 to Rs 1.25 lakh per worker.

Nahar said all sectors, from automobiles to electrical and electronic goods, had good order books and that factories were working to complete orders on time. The bonus money is also flowing into gold, home appliances and real estate, alongside the traditional festive purchases.

Garments first, cars on the first visit

"The market rush has increased since Sunday."

— Naresh Parakh, President, Nashik Retail Cloth Merchants' Association

Naresh Parakh, president of the Nashik Retail Cloth Merchants' Association, said garment-store footfall rose from November 1, once bonuses were disbursed. He added that shoppers are cautious because of inflation, and that while good Diwali business is expected, it may come in lower than last year.

Automobile dealers reported the same pattern. Sachin Mahajan, Maharashtra president of the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA), said competitive prices and festive dealer offers were supporting vehicle sales, with the bonus encouraging customers to upgrade or replace their vehicles. Buyer behaviour has changed too, he said: customers who once visited, checked vehicles and took time before booking now often book on the very first visit.

For the diaspora reader with family in Nashik, the picture is a familiar one: the festive economy runs on the industrial estates. When Satpur and Ambad pay well, Main Road feels it within days.
